object_description: pavilion complex with a workshop character and shed roofs, opened towards the stream
design_condition: the pavilion complex is developed from the context with a connection to the stream, merging the exterior space along the water with the interior and defining a commons-like outdoor area to the south

positive: The project is sensitively developed from the context and enhances the site with the chosen typology
The school building creates a sense of identity, marks the public character and is characterised by a clear idea
Designing the school as a pavilion complex with a connection to the stream is convincing
The address and the entrance situations are clear and natural
The idea of a school with a workshop character referencing the factory buildings is interesting and innovative
It enables new pedagogical forms of learning
The merging of the exterior space along the stream with the interior is of particular interest
Widening and nature-oriented measures let users experience the project-defining stream
The careful design of the riverbank area and the commons-like southern outdoor space have spatial qualities
The relationship to the existing upper school building is reinforced and emphasised by a new footpath
The learning landscapes as an open structure offer a wide range of options for new forms of teaching
The proposed measures for room partitions are plausible and emphasise the workshop character
The vertical spatial connections created by the staircases are attractive and enhance the spatial experience
The chosen timber construction is self-explanatory, sustainable, well-founded and carefully developed
The foundation concept is plausible and shows intensive examination of statics and building ground
The inhabited shell is congruent with the floor plan typology and suggests a stimulating spatial atmosphere
Materialisation and raw construction are sustainable and energetically sensible
The quality of light on the upper floor is improved by eastern orientation and zenithal light from the shed roofs
The project impresses with its contextual, conceptual and spatial qualities
It represents a promising spatial offer for the desired forms of learning
negative: The imposing size of the volume requires an approach that cannot be derived from familiar school examples
It leads to forms of use that would have to be relearned by teaching staff and pupils
Whether the stream experience actually works in everyday school life is questioned
The proposed amount of space is lavishly large
It requires teachers to develop teaching skills that cannot be taken for granted
The very large footprint results in a higher cubature
Whether prefabrication and structure can offset the high costs of the larger cubature is difficult to say
The location of the garage ramp is unsatisfactory and protrudes into the current street bay
The orientation of the classrooms to the west and north-west is not optimal
The lighting conditions on the ground floor are not convincing and are called into question
The options for separating recreational areas and learning zones were not shown
The project could not quite meet the high architectural and functional requirements
